statement: Let V = {1,2,...,n}. A valid schedule with m semesters is a function A: V -> {1,2,...,m} such that (i) for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), A(relations[i][0]) < A(relations[i][1]), and (ii) for every s with 1 <= s <= m, the number of courses c in V with A(c) = s is at most k. The function returns a result r and r is the least integer m >= 1 for which a valid schedule with m semesters exists.
preconditions: Let n_val and k_val be the integer values of the parameters n and k. Assume: 1 <= n_val <= 15; 1 <= k_val <= n_val; relations is a slice of vectors of Int64 with 0 <= len(relations) <= n_val*(n_val-1)/2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2, 1 <= relations[i][0] <= n_val, 1 <= relations[i][1] <= n_val, and relations[i][0] != relations[i][1]; for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(relations), (relations[i][0], relations[i][1]) != (relations[j][0], relations[j][1]); the directed graph on vertices {1,...,n_val} with an edge from relations[i][0] to relations[i][1] for each i is acyclic.

statement: Let V = {1,2,...,n}. The function returns a result r and there exists a function A: V -> {1,2,...,r} such that (i) for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), A(relations[i][0]) < A(relations[i][1]), and (ii) for every s with 1 <= s <= r, the number of courses c in V with A(c) = s is at most k. Thus r semesters are sufficient.

statement: Let L be the largest integer t such that there exist distinct courses v_1, ..., v_t in {1,...,n} with, for every j with 1 <= j < t, the pair (v_j, v_{j+1}) occurs in relations (i.e., there is an edge from v_j to v_{j+1}). statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for any slice relations' of vectors of Int64 (with the same n and k) satisfying the same preconditions such that the transitive closure of the edge set of relations' on {1,...,n} equals the transitive closure of the edge set of relations, the function applied to (n, relations', k) also returns r. The transitive closure is the set of pairs (a,b) such that there is a directed path of length at least 1 from a to b.

statement: Whenever the function applied to (n, relations, k) returns r and the function applied to (n, relations', k) returns r', then r' >= r. Adding prerequisite edges cannot reduce the minimum number of semesters.
preconditions: Let n_val and k_val be the integer values of the parameters n and k. Assume: 1 <= n_val <= 15; 1 <= k_val <= n_val; relations is a slice of vectors of Int64 with 0 <= len(relations) <= n_val*(n_val-1)/2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2, 1 <= relations[i][0] <= n_val, 1 <= relations[i][1] <= n_val, and relations[i][0] != relations[i][1]; for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(relations), (relations[i][0], relations[i][1]) != (relations[j][0], relations[j][1]); the directed graph on vertices {1,...,n_val} with an edge from relations[i][0] to relations[i][1] for each i is acyclic. Let relations' be another slice of vectors of Int64 satisfying the same structural preconditions, with the additional condition that every pair (relations[i][0], relations[i][1]) occurring in relations also occurs as some pair (relations'[j][0], relations'[j][1]) in relations'.

statement: Whenever the function applied to (n, relations, k) returns r and the function applied to (n, relations', k) returns r', then r' = r. The answer is invariant under relabeling courses.
preconditions: Let n_val and k_val be the integer values of the parameters n and k. Assume: 1 <= n_val <= 15; 1 <= k_val <= n_val; relations is a slice of vectors of Int64 with 0 <= len(relations) <= n_val*(n_val-1)/2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2, 1 <= relations[i][0] <= n_val, 1 <= relations[i][1] <= n_val, and relations[i][0] != relations[i][1]; for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(relations), (relations[i][0], relations[i][1]) != (relations[j][0], relations[j][1]); the directed graph on vertices {1,...,n_val} with an edge from relations[i][0] to relations[i][1] for each i is acyclic. Let pi : {1,...,n_val} -> {1,...,n_val} be a bijection, and let relations' be any slice of vectors of Int64 satisfying the same structural preconditions obtained by replacing each occurrence of a pair [a,b] in relations with [pi(a),pi(b)] and listing the resulting pairs in any order.

statement: Let L be the largest integer t such that there exist distinct courses v_1, ..., v_t in {1,...,n} with, for every j with 1 <= j < t, the pair (v_j, v_{j+1}) occurs in relations. Let W be the largest integer w such that there exist courses c_1, ..., c_w in {1,...,n} that are pairwise incomparable with respect to the transitive closure of the edge set of relations, i.e. for every distinct i, j neither (c_i,c_j) nor (c_j,c_i) belongs to the transitive closure. Whenever the function returns a result r and k >= W, then r = L.
